title: Pulsewave rollout checklist and cadence notes (Jan 2025)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist + cadence notes for the Pulsewave feature small-batch rollout. Goal is low-risk exposure for canary cohort, clear telemetry anchors, and a fast rollforward/rollback path if model-serving or latency regressions appear.

Scope:
- Applies to: hosted API route /v1/pulsewave, dedicated pools using waveform-v2, and rip-and-redeploy on private deployments for customers who opt in.
- Not covered: schema changes to client SDKs (separate SDK compatibility release).

Quick summary (one-liner):
- 4-week gradual ramp: day-of micro-canaries -> week-of cohort ramps -> 3-week scaled validation -> full cutover.
- Primary risks: tail latency regressions, KV cache invalidation, incorrect fallback mapping.

High-level roles & contacts (day-of ops):
- Release owner: Leah Kim (primary contact)
- Canary shepherd: Miguel Hernandez (observability + traffic routing)
- Telemetry lead: Priya Shah (dashboard + alerts)
- Rollback/infra lead: Tom Bowers (capacity, infra actions)
- Customer comms/CS: Ivy Chen
- On-call escalation: SRE rotation (see team roster)

Calendar & cadence (rough):
Week -2 (prep) -- Jan 10–16
- Finalize canary cohort list (5% of traffic for selected internal shards).
- Bake smoke-runner job: endpoint smoke-runner/pulsewave-smoke-v1 (run locally & in staging).
- Generate canary prompt set (50 prompts) and baseline outputs (golden set).
- TODO: confirm dedicated pool sizing for burst capacity. (Action: Tom)

Week -1 (preflight) -- Jan 17–23
- Run soak tests in staging (48h).
- Telemetry dashboards: add anchors (p95 latency, tail 99.9, error-rate, tokens/sec per route).
- Run A/B for small internal cohort (10 internal customers).
- Validate fallback mapping matrix (waveform-v2 -> waveform-v1).

Day 0 (canary) -- Jan 24
- Deploy to canary pools (label: pulsewave/canary-2025-01-24).
- Start 5% traffic routing for 2 hours -> automated smoke run -> expand to 15% for 6 hours if green.
- Checkpoints at +15m, +60m, +180m.
- If any critical alerts fire, immediate rollback instructions executed (see Rollback triggers).

Week 1 (cohort ramp) -- Jan 25–31
- Gradual increase: 25% day 1, 50% day 3, 75% day 5.
- Manual sign-off at 50% by Release owner + Telemetry lead.
- Run regression evals daily against golden set (quality regression threshold: BLEU-like score drop <= 0.8% and safety triggers none).

Weeks 2–4 (scaled validation) -- Feb 1–21
- Monitor throughput and caching effects on latency.
- Enable cache warmers for top-100 prefixes.
- Run edge-case fuzzing job twice per week.
- Final go/no-go discussion at end of week 4 for full cutover.

Preflight checklist (quick run before Day 0):
- [ ] Release notes drafted and published internally (owner: Leah)
- [ ] Canary cohort list confirmed (Miguel)
- [ ] Staging soak passed (Priya)
- [ ] Telemetry anchors instrumented and tested (Priya)
- [ ] Capacity runway validated + burst plan (Tom)
- [ ] Rollback artifact (previous model bundle) staged and smoke-tested (Tom)
- [ ] Customer comms drafted (Ivy)
- [ ] Feature flags in place (toggle: pulsewave.rollout)
- [ ] Automated smoke-runner jobs scheduled (CI)
- [ ] On-call notified and calendar invite created

Day-of Operator checklist (Minute-level):
T-60m
- Confirm deploy artifact hash and manifests.
- Post initial note to #release-ops with manifest and canary targets.

T+0
- Kick off canary rollout; confirm route tables updated.
- Start baseline smoke-runner.
- Watch dashboard panel: latency p95, 99.9, errors/min, model-fallback-count.

T+15m
- Quick sanity check, confirm no spike in errors or unusual latencies.
- Annotate any anomalies in the release log.

T+60m
- Evaluate telemetry: if p99 increased > 20% or errors > 0.5% absolute (from baseline) -> hold and notify rollback lead.

T+180m
- If still green, proceed to 15% -> continue cadence as planned.

Smoke tests (automated):
- Basic correctness: run golden prompt set, diff outputs, flag >0.8% metric drift.
- Latency regression: measure cold and warm tail latencies; compare to baseline.
- KV cache verification: prefix cache hit ratio should not drop below 70% after warmers.
- Safety / policy checks: content classifier pass rate should be 100% for test set.

Telemetry anchors & dashboards (must be ready):
- p95 latency (route: /v1/pulsewave)
- p99 and p99.9 tail latency (separate panels for cold vs warm requests)
- Error rate per minute (5m, 1m)
- Fallback rate (count of requests falling back to waveform-v1)
- Model output divergence score (daily aggregated reg metric)
- Token throughput (tokens/sec per pool)
- Cache hit ratio (kv-cache)

Rollback / Rollforward triggers (decision heuristics):
High-severity immediate rollback (must rollback within 15m):
- Any availability impact affecting >1% of customer traffic (service errors >= 5% for 5 minutes).
- Consistent p99 > 2x baseline sustained for 30 minutes.
- Safety classifier failure (any hit on high-risk prompts)

Medium-severity hold + deeper triage (pause ramp, notify teams):
- Error rate increased by >0.5% absolute for 20 minutes.
- Output divergence metric > 2% and manual inspection shows clear degradations.
- Cache invalidation issues causing sustained cold tails beyond 45 minutes.

Low-severity (observe, telemetry-only):
- Minor quality drift within tolerance, small latency upticks <15%.

Rollback steps (quick):
1) Flip feature flag pulsewave.rollout -> previous variant.
2) Re-route traffic in control-plane to waveform-v1 pools.
3) Notify #release-ops + SRE + Product.
4) Start post-rollback verification smoke-runner (15m).
5) Create incident ticket and run RCA cadence if >5% customer impact.

Pre-defined fallbacks (coded into router):
- waveform-v2 -> waveform-v1 (no stateful migration required).
- If dedicated pool capacity under pressure, route to hosted cold pool with reduced token cap.

Comms templates (short):
- Internal alert (short): "Pulsewave canary detected elevated p99 at T+60m. Holding ramp. Release owner: Leah. Rollback lead: Tom. See RND-4321 for details."
- Customer facing (if rollback required): "We paused a rollout of Pulsewave due to observed latency issues. We're reverting to the prior configuration while we investigate. No customer data was impacted. ETA for follow-up: 2 hours."

Post-release notes (to be filled):
- Final rollout windows and percent exposure timeline.
- Regression numbers (latency, errors, divergence) vs baseline.
- Lessons learned + follow-ups.

Postmortem template (populate after incident):
- Summary (what happened):
- Timeline (minute-level):
- Impact: customers affected, duration, customer-visible symptoms.
- Root cause hypothesis:
- Remediation actions: short-term & long-term.
- Owners and ETA for follow-ups.

Open questions / things to decide (brain dump):
- Should we include a second canary cohort in a different region simultaneously? Pros: catch region-specific infra issues. Cons: doubles ops overhead. (leaning yes for critical infra).
- Acceptance threshold for divergence: current default 0.8% — is that conservative enough for Pulsewave? Priya to propose updated metric by Jan 16.
- How much of the golden prompt set should be synthetic vs real traffic replays? Need product input.
- Need to confirm whether private deployment customers will be auto-opted into the rollout or require explicit opt-in. (Action: Ivy)

Notes to self / quick scratch:
- If rollback happens after 75% ramp, be prepared for cache coldness on v1 -> expect tail p99 spike for ~20–30m. Pre-warm steps ahead of rollback? possible but risky.
- TODO: add checklist step to verify router mapping within 5 minutes of deploy (small script ready).

Appendix: useful commands / links
- Router re-route CLI: infractl route update --service pulsewave --target canary-2025-01-24
- Smoke-runner: ci/pulsewave-smoke-runner.sh --env=staging --set=golden-set.json
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Playbook

Last thoughts:
This doc is intentionally lean — it should be copied into the release binder and expanded with the final customer comms. Keep telemetry thresholds visible and ask Telemetry lead to proactively watch the p99 tail during ramp.

-- Leah
